blocks.text: A volume is data on one host's disk, not a backup; use logical dumps for databases and stopped-writer file copies for everything else.

$ docker compose exec -T db pg_dump -U app -d rag -Fc > backups/rag.dump
$ docker compose exec -T db pg_restore -U app -d rag --clean --if-exists < backups/rag.dump

items: Consistent while running, portable across versions.
`-T` is mandatory: a TTY corrupts binary output.
Qdrant: use its snapshot API, not live file copies.

blocks.text:
$ docker compose stop db
$ docker run --rm -v rag_pgdata:/data:ro -v "$PWD/backups:/backup" alpine tar czf /backup/pgdata.tgz -C /data .
$ docker compose start db
$ docker volume create rag_pgdata_restored
$ docker run --rm -v rag_pgdata_restored:/data -v "$PWD/backups:/backup" alpine tar xzf /backup/pgdata.tgz -C /data
Copying a live database's files gives a crash-consistent copy at best, a corrupt one at worst.

Q: "How do you back up a Postgres container?" A: "pg_dump via exec -T on a schedule, stored off-host and encrypted if sensitive, with a retention policy and regularly tested restores. File-level volume copies only with the database stopped, and only for the same major version."
